scope: Scene04 canonical source and scene-local review only
comparisonObservations: The old native full-frame hall silhouette already occupies approximately the reference width; arbitrary camera widening or enlargement would damage the path/stair/lantern correspondence.

The old porch reads as two narrow same-depth horizontal strips over shafts, with a dark lattice-like vault. Reference mass comes from thick shaped transfer members, bearings and deep warm nested timber under the curved roof.
The old roof barrel units meet end to end with a gap. Reference ceramic courses visibly overlap and carry substantial curved end lips.
The old gold figure is low and squat in the opening; the reference figure is slimmer and higher on a raised altar, within a more occupied carved recess.
The old material produces broad artificial pale patches in the shaft close view. The repository contains a licensed CC0 timber scan suitable for a separate material revision.

geometryChanges: Upper and lower shaped beam heights 0.48/0.44m to 0.62/0.57m; actual fore-aft depth 0.50m to 0.80m.
Lower nuki plane moved from z=0.85m to z=0.22m, leaving actual parallax beneath the upper transfer.
Central turned shaft bearing datum raised by 0.26m; actual orthogonal deep receiving arms, blocks and rear return beams added.
Four deep curved vault carriers and four side-bay bearing headers added as closed extruded solids.
Main and canopy ceramic units genuinely overlap, with larger front barrel sections and independent tail rise.
Four framed floral lattice centres added behind the columns.
Sanctuary canopy/dais raised 0.55m, figure slimmed and raised on a joined high pedestal, lamps positioned beside the torso.
findings: Two transfers are heavier and shrine figure is better placed, but the shoulder wall stays flat and the side galleries remain too low.
Rectangular gold plaque/collar forms persist; wood is too pale and uneven in the genuine hero view.
Full and hero native buffers are both 1254x1254 with no upscaling; runtime errors empty.
Real deep frame/reveal/roof parallax is visible in the native low oblique; right rear roof height is improved.
Return galleries sit too far outward and expose bare toy-like gallery walls.
Raised far hill shows pale angular crown blobs; flowering cherries remain low bushes instead of the tall reference canopies.
Portal front leaf strip still reads as flat applied gold.
Full native view now has substantial near return roof framing, taller real cherry branches and a fuller carved portal.
Low native oblique retains deep structural/reveal parallax.
Hill crowns still read as large discrete blobs and cherry blooms form too uniform a horizontal band.
Finer real hill clusters and nonuniform cherry branch elevation repair the preceding large-blob/flat-band failures.
Full view retains improved right/back/return roof occupation and the low fixed processional composition.
Hero and low oblique show genuine closed timber/ceramic/reveal geometry and correct raised shrine occupation.

Photographic fidelity is still rejected: timber/roof/carving forms and surface response remain stylized, the botanical canopy and stone-lantern silhouettes differ, and the original photograph has a more integrated warm daylight/micro-shadow response.

limitations: Single-view metric and hidden construction remain authored hypotheses.
Authored carving135 relief and historical generated material guides retain their original provenance.
Valid native geometry and nonempty pixels do not prove photographic fidelity.
No reference-photo RGB, view-facing architecture, AI replacement frame, point cloud or Gaussian splat is used.
